questions.question: A scalar valued function is defined as \(f(x) = x^T A x + b^T x + c\), where \(A\) is a symmetric positive definite matrix with dimension \(n \times n\) ; \(b\) and \(x\) are vectors of dimension \(n \times 1\). The minimum value of \(f(x)\) will occur when \(x\) equals
questions.explanation:
Let \(n = 2\), \[A = \begin{pmatrix} p & q \\ q & r \end{pmatrix}\], \[X = \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix}\], and \[B = \begin{pmatrix} b_1 \\ b_2 \end{pmatrix}\]. The function is defined as: \[f(x) = X^T AX + B^T X + C\] \[\implies f(x) = (px^2 + 2qxy + ry^2) + (b_1 x + b_2 y) + C\] To find the stationary points, we compute the first partial derivatives and set them to zero: \[\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial x} = 0 \implies 2px + 2qy + b_1 = 0 \quad \text{--- (1)}\] \[\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial y} = 0 \implies 2qx + 2ry + b_2 = 0 \quad \text{--- (2)}\] Equations (1) and (2) can be expressed simultaneously in matrix form as: \[2 \begin{pmatrix} p & q \\ q & r \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix} = -\begin{pmatrix} b_1 \\ b_2 \end{pmatrix}\] \[\implies 2AX = -B\] \[\implies AX = -\dfrac{B}{2}\] \[\therefore X = -\dfrac{A^{-1}B}{2} \quad \text{--- (3)}\] Since matrix \(A\) is given to be positive definite, its determinant is strictly positive (\(|A| > 0\)) and its leading principal minors are positive (\(p > 0\)). To check for a maximum or minimum, we evaluate the second-order partial derivatives: \[\text{rt} - s^2 = 4(pr - q^2) > 0\] Since \(|A| = pr - q^2 > 0\) and \(r = 2p > 0\), the discriminant condition \(\text{rt} - s^2 > 0\) with \(r > 0\) confirms a local minimum. \[\therefore \text{At } X = -\dfrac{A^{-1}B}{2} \text{ we get the minimum of } f(x).\] Similarly, this multi-variable minimization property holds true for \(n > 2\). \[\boxed{\text{(C) $-\left(\dfrac{A^{-1} b}{2}\right)$}}\]
Key points
  • Matrix Differentiation: The gradient of the quadratic form \(X^T AX + B^T X + C\) with respect to vector \(X\) is given by \(2AX + B = 0\).
  • Optimality Condition: If the Hessian matrix (which is \(2A\)) is positive definite, the stationary point corresponds to a strict global minimum.
Mistakes to avoid
  • Incorrect Sign During Matrix Inversion: Forgetting to switch the sign of vector \(B\) when moving it to the right-hand side, leading to \(X = \dfrac{A^{-1}B}{2}\) instead of the correct negative value.
  • Misinterpreting Positive Definiteness: Confusing positive definite properties with maximum value conditions. Remember that a positive definite Hessian matrix always implies a local minimum, not a maximum.
  • Missing the Scaling Factor: Omitting the factor of \(2\) when differentiating the quadratic term \(X^T AX\), which leads to an incorrect stationary point of \(X = -A^{-1}B\).

questions.question:
Given \[\begin{aligned}
    x(t) &= 3 \sin (1000\pi t) \quad \text{and} \\
    y(t) &= 5\cos \left( 1000\pi t + \frac{\pi}{4} \right)
\end{aligned}\] The x-yplot will be
questions.explanation:
Let \(\phi = 1000\pi t\). The parametric equations are given by: \[x = 3 \sin \phi \implies rac{x}{3} = \sin \phi \quad ext{--- (1)}\] \[y = 5 \cos\left(\phi + rac{\pi}{4} ight)\] Using the trigonometric identity \(\cos(A + B) = \cos A \cos B - \sin A \sin B\): \[ rac{y}{5} = \cos \phi \cos\left( rac{\pi}{4} ight) - \sin \phi \sin\left( rac{\pi}{4} ight)\] \[ rac{y}{5} = rac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \cos \phi - rac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \sin \phi\] Substituting equation (1) into the expression: \[ rac{y}{5} = rac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \left( \cos \phi - rac{x}{3} ight)\] \[ rac{\sqrt{2}}{5}y = \cos \phi - rac{x}{3}\] \[ rac{x}{3} + rac{\sqrt{2}}{5}y = \cos \phi \quad ext{--- (2)}\] Squaring and adding equations (1) and (2) to eliminate \(\phi\): \[\left(\sin \phi ight)^2 + \left(\cos \phi ight)^2 = \left( rac{x}{3} ight)^2 + \left( rac{x}{3} + rac{\sqrt{2}}{5}y ight)^2\] \[1 = rac{x^2}{9} + rac{x^2}{9} + rac{2\sqrt{2}}{15}xy + rac{2}{25}y^2\] \[ rac{2x^2}{9} + rac{2\sqrt{2}}{15}xy + rac{2}{25}y^2 - 1 = 0 \quad ext{--- (3)}\] The general second-degree equation is of the form: \[ax^2 + 2hxy + by^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\] Comparing this with equation (3), we get: \[a = rac{2}{9}, \quad h = rac{\sqrt{2}}{15}, \quad b = rac{2}{25}, \quad g = 0, \quad f = 0, \quad c = -1\] To determine the type of conic section, we evaluate the discriminant \(ab - h^2\): \[ab - h^2 = \left( rac{2}{9} ight)\left( rac{2}{25} ight) - \left( rac{\sqrt{2}}{15} ight)^2\] \[ab - h^2 = rac{4}{225} - rac{2}{225} = rac{2}{225} > 0\] Since \(ab - h^2 > 0\), the equation represents either an ellipse or a point. Let us check the determinant \(\Delta\): \[\Delta = egin{vmatrix} a & h & g \ h & b & f \ g & f & c \end{vmatrix} = egin{vmatrix} rac{2}{9} & rac{\sqrt{2}}{15} & 0 \ rac{\sqrt{2}}{15} & rac{2}{25} & 0 \ 0 & 0 & -1 \end{vmatrix} = -1 \left( ab - h^2 ight) = - rac{2}{225} eq 0\] Since \(\Delta eq 0\) and \(ab - h^2 > 0\), the curve is a non-degenerate ellipse. \[ oxed{ ext{(d) an ellipse}}\]
Key points
For any general second-degree equation \(ax^2 + 2hxy + by^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0\), with \(\Delta eq 0\):
  • If \(h^2 - ab < 0\) (or \(ab - h^2 > 0\)), it represents an ellipse.
  • If \(h^2 - ab = 0\), it represents a parabola.
  • If \(h^2 - ab > 0\), it represents a hyperbola.

questions.question: The figure shows the schematic of a production process with machines \(A\), \(B\) and \(C\). An input job needs to be pre-processed either by \(A\) or by \(B\) before it is fed to \(C\), from which the final finished product comes out. The probabilities of failure of the machines are given as \[P_A = 0.15,\qquad P_B = 0.05,\qquad P_C = 0.1.\] Assuming independence of failures of the machines, the probability that a given job is successfully processed (up to the third decimal place) is .
questions.explanation:
For successful processing, machine \(C\) must work and at least one of \(A\) or \(B\) must work. \[P(\text{A and B fail})=P_A P_B=(0.15)(0.05)=0.0075\] \[P(\text{at least one of A or B works}) =1-0.0075=0.9925\] \[P(C\text{ works})=1-P_C=1-0.1=0.9\] Hence, \[P(\text{successful processing}) =0.9925\times 0.9 =0.89325\] \[\boxed{0.893}\]
Key points
  • Parallel stage (\(A\) and \(B\)): system works if at least one machine works.
  • Series stage with \(C\): overall success probability is the product of stage success probabilities.

questions.question: The iteration step in order to solve for the cube roots of a given number '\(N\)' using the Newton-Raphson's method is
questions.explanation:
We want to find the cube root of a given number \(N\) using the Newton-Raphson method. This can be modeled as finding the root of the equation: \[x = \sqrt[3]{N} \implies x^3 = N \implies f(x) = x^3 - N = 0\] Take the first derivative of \(f(x)\) with respect to \(x\): \[f'(x) = 3x^2\] The standard Newton-Raphson iteration formula is: \[x_{k+1} = x_k - \dfrac{f(x_k)}{f'(x_k)}\] Substitute \(f(x_k)\) and \(f'(x_k)\) into the recurrence relation: \[x_{k+1} = x_k - \dfrac{x_k^3 - N}{3x_k^2}\] Combine the terms over a common denominator: \[\begin{aligned} x_{k+1} &= \dfrac{x_k \left(3x_k^2\right) - \left(x_k^3 - N\right)}{3x_k^2} \\[1.5ex] &= \dfrac{3x_k^3 - x_k^3 + N}{3x_k^2} \\[1.5ex] &= \dfrac{2x_k^3 + N}{3x_k^2} \\[1.5ex] &= \dfrac{1}{3} \left( 2x_k + \dfrac{N}{x_k^2} \right) \end{aligned}\] This structural updating relation matches Option B. \[\boxed{\text{B. } x_{k+1} = \dfrac{1}{3}\left(2x_k + \dfrac{N}{x_k^2}\right)}\]
Key points
  • General Power Root Recurrence: The generalized Newton-Raphson updating format for finding the \(p^{\text{th}}\) root of a number \(N\) simplifies cleanly to: \[x_{k+1} = \dfrac{1}{p} \left[ (p-1)x_k + \dfrac{N}{x_k^{p-1}} \right]\]

questions.question: \(X(k)\) is the Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) of a 6-point real sequence \(x(n)\). If \(X(0)=9+j0,\) \(X(2)=2+j2,\) \(X(3)=3-j0,\) \(X(5)=1-j1,\) then \(x(0)\) is
questions.explanation:
Theory: For a real-valued sequence,\[X(k)=X^{*}(N-k).\]Also,\[x(n)=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}X(k)e^{j\frac{2\pi kn}{N}}.\]Given,\[N=6,\]\[X(0)=9,\qquad X(2)=2+j2,\qquad X(3)=3,\qquad X(5)=1-j.\]Using conjugate symmetry,\[X(1)=X^{*}(5)=1+j,\]\[X(4)=X^{*}(2)=2-j2.\]For \(n=0\),\[x(0) = \frac16 \sum_{k=0}^{5}X(k).\]Therefore,\[\begin{aligned} x(0) &= \frac16 \left[ 9+(1+j)+(2+j2)+3+(2-j2)+(1-j) \right] \\ &= \frac16(18)\\ &=3. \end{aligned}\] \[\boxed{\text{(A) }3}\]
Key points
  • For real sequences, \(X(k)=X^{*}(N-k)\).
  • At \(n=0\), all IDFT exponential terms become unity.
  • Sum all DFT coefficients before dividing by \(N\).
Mistakes to avoid
  • Do not forget to determine the missing DFT coefficients using conjugate symmetry.
  • Remember that \(X(0)\) and \(X(N/2)\) are purely real for real sequences.
  • Divide the final sum by \(N\).

questions.question: A discrete-time signal \(x[n]\) is obtained by sampling an analog signal at \(10~\text{kHz}\). The signal \(x[n]\) is filtered by a system with impulse response\[h[n]=0.5\,[\delta[n]+\delta[n-1]].\]The \(3\) dB cut-off frequency of the filter is
questions.explanation:
Theory: The frequency response is obtained by taking the DTFT of the impulse response. Given,\[h[n]=0.5\,[\delta[n]+\delta[n-1]].\]Hence,\[H\!\left(e^{j\Omega}\right) = 0.5\left(1+e^{-j\Omega}\right).\]Its magnitude is\[\left|H\!\left(e^{j\Omega}\right)\right| = \frac{1}{2} \sqrt{(1+\cos\Omega)^2+\sin^2\Omega}.\]Using\[(1+\cos\Omega)^2+\sin^2\Omega = 2+2\cos\Omega = 4\cos^2\!\left(\frac{\Omega}{2}\right),\]we obtain\[\left|H\!\left(e^{j\Omega}\right)\right| = \cos\left(\frac{\Omega}{2}\right).\]At the \(3\) dB cut-off frequency,\[\left|H\!\left(e^{j\Omega_c}\right)\right| = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}.\]Therefore,\[\cos\left(\frac{\Omega_c}{2}\right) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\]which gives\[\frac{\Omega_c}{2} = \frac{\pi}{4} \quad\Rightarrow\quad \Omega_c = \frac{\pi}{2}.\]Since \[2\pi\ \text{rad/sample} \longleftrightarrow 10~\text{kHz},\]the corresponding analog frequency is\[f_c = \frac{\Omega_c}{2\pi}f_s = \frac{\pi/2}{2\pi}\times10 = 2.5~\text{kHz}.\]Hence,\[\boxed{\text{(B) }2.50~\text{kHz}}\]
Key points
  • Obtain the DTFT of the impulse response before finding the cut-off frequency.
  • Use the identity \(2+2\cos\Omega=4\cos^2(\Omega/2)\).
  • Convert normalized frequency to analog frequency using \(f=\dfrac{\Omega}{2\pi}f_s\).
Mistakes to avoid
  • Do not equate the \(3\) dB point to \(\Omega=\pi/4\); the correct value is \(\Omega=\pi/2\).
  • Do not forget to convert from rad/sample to Hz.
  • Use the magnitude response, not the complex frequency response, for determining the cut-off frequency.

questions.explanation: The Zener diode fixes the base voltage at \[V_{B}=V_{Z}=15\,\text{V}\] Since the transistor is an emitter follower, \[V_{E}=V_{B}+V_{BE}=15+0.7=15.7\,\text{V}\] The load current through the \(100\,\Omega\) resistor is \[I_{E}=\frac{15.7}{100} =157\,\text{mA}\] Using \[I_{E}=(\beta+1)I_{B}, \qquad \beta=40\] \[I_{B}=\frac{157}{41} =3.83\,\text{mA}\] The current through the \(330\,\Omega\) resistor is \[I_{R}=\frac{30-15}{330} =\frac{15}{330} =45.45\,\text{mA}\] Applying KCL at the base node, \[I_{R}=I_{Z}+I_{B}\] \[I_{Z}=45.45-3.83 =41.62\,\text{mA}\] \[\boxed{41.62}\]

questions.explanation: Quantisation noise power = \(\dfrac{\Delta^2}{12}\) , where \(\Delta\) = step size. Step size is defined as: \[\Delta = \frac{V}{2^N-1}\] \[\therefore \text{Quantisation noise power = } \frac{\Delta^2}{12} = \frac{V^2}{12(2^N-1)^2}\] \[\boxed{(A) \; \frac{V^2}{12(2^N-1)^2}}\]

questions.subject: control-systems
questions.ref: Block Diagram and Signal Flow Graph Q1
questions.question: Consider the control system shown in figurewith feedforwardaction for rejection of a measurable disturbance \(d(t)\). The value of \(K\), for whichthe disturbance response at the output \(y(t)\) is zero mean, is:
questions.explanation:
Method 1
Using block diagram algebraic reduction equations directly at the summing nodes: \[Y(s) = \left[-50Y(s) + KD(s)\right]\frac{1}{s + 2} + D(s)\] Grouping \(Y(s)\) and \(D(s)\) terms: \[Y(s)\left[1 + \frac{50}{s + 2}\right] = \left[\frac{K}{s + 2} + 1\right]D(s)\] \[Y(s)\left[\frac{s + 52}{s + 2}\right] = \left[\frac{K + s + 2}{s + 2}\right]D(s)\] \[Y(s) = \frac{K + s + 2}{s + 52}D(s)\] Converting to the frequency domain (\(s = j\omega\)): \[Y(j\omega) = \frac{K + j\omega + 2}{j\omega + 52}D(j\omega)\] For the output to have a zero mean value, the response at \(\omega = 0\) must satisfy \(Y(j0) = 0\): \[\frac{K + j0 + 2}{j0 + 52}D(j0) = 0\] \[\frac{K + 2}{52} = 0 \implies K = -2\]
Method 2
Using Mason's Gain Formula for the transfer function \(T(s) = \dfrac{Y(s)}{D(s)}\) with \(r(t) = 0\): \[T(s) = \frac{\sum P_i \Delta_i}{\Delta}\] Forward Paths from \(D(s)\) to \(Y(s)\):
\[P_1 = 1, \quad \Delta_1 = 1; \ \ and \quad P_2 = \frac{K}{s + 2}, \quad \Delta_2 = 1\] Feedback Loops:
\(L_1 = -50 \cdot \left(\dfrac{1}{s + 2}\right) = -\dfrac{50}{s + 2}\) Determinant: \(\Delta = 1 - L_1 = 1 + \dfrac{50}{s + 2} = \dfrac{s + 52}{s + 2}\) Evaluating the transfer function: \[T(s) = \dfrac{1 + \dfrac{K}{s + 2}}{\dfrac{s + 52}{s + 2}} = \frac{s + 2 + K}{s + 52}\] For a zero-mean steady-state output, the DC gain must be zero (\(s = 0\)): \[T(0) = 0\] \[\frac{2 + K}{52} = 0 \implies K = -2\]
\[\boxed{(D) \ \ -2}\]
Key points
Complete disturbance rejection or zero-mean output tracking under constant inputs is achieved when the closed-loop system transmission zeros neutralize the input poles at \(\omega = 0\).

questions.subject: control-systems
questions.question: A plant has an open-loop transfer function, \[G_p(s) = \frac{20}{(s+0.1)(s+2)(s+100)}.\] The approximate model obtained by retaining only one of the above poles, which is closest to the frequency response of the original transfer function at low frequency is
questions.explanation:
At low frequencies (\(\omega \to 0\)), the Laplace variable \(s = j\omega \to 0\). The low-frequency response is dominated by the pole closest to the origin. \[G_p(s) = \frac{20}{(s+0.1)(s+2)(s+100)}\] The poles of the system are located at \(s = -0.1\), \(s = -2\), and \(s = -100\). The dominant pole nearest to the origin is at \(s = -0.1\). To approximate the model by retaining only this dominant pole while keeping the low-frequency steady-state gain unchanged, we approximate the insignificant high-frequency poles by setting \(s \to 0\) in those terms: \[G_p(s) \approx \frac{20}{(s+0.1) \times 2 \times 100} = \frac{20}{200(s+0.1)} = \frac{0.1}{s+0.1}\] \[\boxed{(A) \ \ \dfrac{0.1}{s+0.1}}\]
Key points
  • Dominant Poles: Poles closer to the imaginary axis dominate the transient response as they have larger time constants.
  • Insignificant Poles: Poles located far to the left (typically \(>5\) times the real part of dominant poles) can be neglected.
Mistakes to avoid
Do not simply remove the other terms without normalizing the numerator; failing to account for the gain will result in an incorrect steady-state value.

questions.explanation:
Given the loop transfer function: \(G(s)H(s) = \dfrac{K(s + 2)}{s^2(s + 10)}\)
  • Poles (\(P\)): \(s = 0, 0, -10 \implies \text{Number of poles } (n) = 3\)
  • Zeros (\(Z\)): \(s = -2 \implies \text{Number of zeros } (m) = 1\)

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: A student is required to demonstrate a high level of <u>comprehension</u> of the subject, especially in the social sciences. The word closest in meaning to <u>comprehension</u> is
questions.explanation:
The sentence states that a student must demonstrate a high level of comprehension of a subject. In this context, comprehension refers to the capacity to grasp, process, and mentally perceive the nature or meaning of the material being studied. Among the given options:
  • Understanding: This is a direct synonym for comprehension, representing the ability to perceive meaning or explain concepts.
  • Meaning: This refers to the definition or significance of a word or concept rather than the act of grasping it.
  • Concentration: This refers to the level of focus or attention applied, which is a prerequisite for comprehension but not the comprehension itself.
  • Stability: This refers to being firm or unchanging, which is unrelated to the cognitive process of learning.
\[\boxed{\text{A. Understanding}}\]
Key points
  • Vocabulary in Context: Selecting the correct synonym requires analyzing how the word functions within the specific sentence.
  • Comprehension: Defined as the power of understanding or the mental grasping of ideas.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Choose the most appropriate word from the options given below to complete the following sentence. One of his biggest ______ was his ability to forgive.
questions.explanation:
The sentence describes "his ability to forgive," which is a positive moral trait. The phrase "One of his biggest..." functions as a superlative structure that must be followed by a plural noun.
  • virtues: This is the plural form of "virtue," referring to behavior showing high moral standards. Forgiveness is fundamentally a moral virtue.
  • vice: This refers to a moral fault or bad habit, which is the antonym of the trait described.
  • choices: While forgiveness involves a choice, "virtues" is the standard categorical term for moral excellences.
  • strength: Although forgiveness is a strength, this word is singular and fails the grammatical requirement for a plural noun.
\[\boxed{\text{B: vice} }\]
Key points
  • Grammatical Agreement: The construction "One of the [Superlative]..." always requires a plural countable noun.
  • Contextual Connotation: The blank must be filled with a word that matches the positive ethical value of "forgiveness."

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Rajan was not happy that Sajan decided to do the project on his own. On observing his unhappiness, Sajan explained to Rajan that he preferred to work independently. Which one of the statements below is logically valid and can be inferred from the above sentences?
options: Rajan has decided to work only in a group.
Rajan and Sajan were formed into a group against their wishes.
Sajan had decided to give in to Rajan's request to work with him.
Rajan had believed that Sajan and he would be working together.
questions.explanation:
The passage establishes that Rajan was unhappy specifically because Sajan decided to work alone. Sajan responded to this unhappiness by explaining his preference for independent work.
  • Option A: The text does not support that Rajan *only* works in groups, just that he was unhappy in this specific instance.
  • Option B: There is no mention of an external force or assignment that placed them in a group against their will.
  • Option C: Sajan "explained" his preference; the text implies he maintained his decision rather than giving in.
  • Option D: If Rajan was unhappy about Sajan working alone, it logically follows that Rajan had expected or assumed they would be working as a pair.
\[\boxed{\text{D: Rajan had believed that Sajan and he would be working together}}\]
Key points
  • Logical Inference: Inferred statements must be direct consequences of the information provided without introducing external assumptions.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Choose the most appropriate word from the options given below to complete the following sentence. A person suffering from Alzheimer’s disease ________ short-term memory loss.
questions.explanation:
The sentence describes a general characteristic or a factual state associated with a medical condition (Alzheimer’s disease). For general truths, habits, or scientific facts, the simple present tense is used.
  • experiences: This is the simple present tense third-person singular form, which correctly matches the subject "A person".
  • experienced: Simple past tense; implies the condition happened only in the past.
  • has experienced: Present perfect tense; suggests an action that happened at an unspecified time before now.
  • is experiencing: Present continuous tense; suggests the action is happening only at this exact moment rather than being a characteristic of the disease.
\[\boxed{\text{D: experiences}}\]
Key points
  • Simple Present Tense: Used to express general truths, permanent situations, or scientific facts.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Choose the most appropriate word from the options given below to complete the following sentence. __________ is the key to their happiness; they are satisfied with what they have.
questions.explanation:
The second part of the sentence states, "they are satisfied with what they have". This context directly defines the missing word.
  • Contentment: The state of being satisfied and happy with one's current situation or possessions.
  • Ambition: A strong desire to achieve something, often implying a lack of satisfaction with the current status.
  • Perseverance: Steadfastness in doing something despite difficulty or delay in achieving success.
  • Hunger: A strong desire or need for something (often food or power), indicating a lack rather than satisfaction.
\[\boxed{\text{A: Contentment}}\]
Key points
  • Contextual Vocabulary: The correct choice must align with the explanatory clause "satisfied with what they have".

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Which of the following options is the closest in meaning to the sentence below? “As a woman, I have no country.”
options: Women are not citizens of any country.
Women’s solidarity knows no national boundaries.
Women of all countries have equal legal rights.
questions.explanation:
The quote "As a woman, I have no country" suggests that the identity and struggles of women transcend national borders and patriotic affiliations.
  • Option C: Suggests that the shared experiences or unity (solidarity) among women are not limited by national boundaries, which aligns with the global perspective of the quote.
  • Option A & B: Take the quote too literally as a statement of statelessness or lack of citizenship.
  • Option D: Discusses legal rights, which is a specific subset of political status not directly captured by the philosophical nature of the quote.
\[\boxed{\text{C:Women’s solidarity knows no national boundaries.}}\]
Key points
  • Critical Thinking: Interpreting philosophical statements requires looking beyond literal meanings to find underlying themes of universal identity or solidarity.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question:
In a group of four children, Som is younger to Riaz. Shiv is elder to Ansu. Ansu is youngest in the group. Which of the following statements is/are required to find the eldest child in the group? Statements
  1. Shiv is younger to Riaz.
  2. Shiv is elder to Som.
options: Statement 1 by itself determines the eldest child.
Statement 2 by itself determines the eldest child.
Statements 1 and 2 are both required to determine the eldest child.
Statements 1 and 2 are not sufficient to determine the eldest child.
questions.explanation:
Given Information: 1. Som \(<\) Riaz 2. Shiv \(>\) Ansu 3. Ansu is the youngest child. From (2) and (3), we know Ansu is at the bottom. We need to find if Riaz or Shiv is at the top. - We have: Riaz \(>\) Som \(>\) Ansu and Shiv \(>\) Ansu. - Statement 1: "Shiv is younger to Riaz" (Riaz > Shiv). Combined with Riaz > Som, this confirms Riaz is the eldest. - Statement 2: "Shiv is elder to Som" (Shiv > Som). This tells us Shiv > Som > Ansu, but we still don't know the relative position of Riaz and Shiv. Therefore, Statement 1 alone is sufficient. \[\boxed{\text{A: Statement 1 by itself determines the eldest child}}\]
Key points
  • Data Sufficiency: Identifying the eldest child requires enough relative comparisons to place one individual above all others in the hierarchy.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Moving into a world of big data will require us to change our thinking about the merits of exactitude. To apply the conventional mindset of measurement to the digital, connected world of the twenty-first century is to miss a crucial point. As mentioned earlier, the obsession with exactness is an artefact of the information-deprived analog era. When data was sparse, every data point was critical, and thus great care was taken to avoid letting any point bias the analysis. From “BIG DATA” Viktor Mayer-Schonberger and Kenneth Cukier The <u>main</u> point of the paragraph is:
options: The twenty-first century is a digital world
Big data is obsessed with exactness
Exactitude is not critical in dealing with big data
Sparse data leads to a bias in the analysis
questions.explanation:
The paragraph argues that while the "analog era" required extreme exactitude due to sparse data, the modern "big data" world requires a change in thinking. It suggests that obsessing over exactness in a digital, connected world is "missing a crucial point". Therefore, the main point is that absolute exactitude is no longer the primary requirement or the most critical factor when dealing with massive datasets. \[\boxed{\text{C:Exactitude is not critical in dealing with big data}}\]
Key points
  • Reading Comprehension: Identifying the core argument involves recognizing the shift in requirements from low-data environments to high-data environments.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Choose the most appropriate phrase from the options given below to complete the following sentence The aircraft ____________ take off as soon as its flight plan was filed.
questions.explanation:
The sentence describes a sequence of events in the past. The second part of the sentence uses the past tense ("was filed"), indicating that the entire action occurred in the past. Therefore, the main clause must also use a past tense form to maintain tense consistency.
  • is allowed to / has been allowed to: These indicate present or ongoing relevance, which conflicts with "was filed."
  • will be allowed to: This indicates a future action.
  • was allowed to: This is the simple past passive form, which correctly aligns with the timeline of the flight plan being filed.
\[\boxed{\text{C: was allowed to}}\]
Key points
  • Tense Consistency: In complex sentences, the tense of the main clause should align with the subordinate clause to establish a logical timeline.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question:
Read the statements:
  • All women are entrepreneurs.
  • Some women are doctors.
Which of the following conclusions can be logically inferred from the above statements?
questions.explanation:
Let \(W\) be the set of women, \(E\) be the set of entrepreneurs, and \(D\) be the set of doctors.
  1. Statement (i) means \(W \subseteq E\) (All women are entrepreneurs).
  2. Statement (ii) means \(W \cap D \neq \emptyset\) (Some women are doctors).
Since some women are doctors and all women are entrepreneurs, there must be a subset of doctors who are also entrepreneurs (specifically, the women who are doctors). Therefore, "Some entrepreneurs are doctors" is the only logical conclusion. \[\boxed{\text{D: Some entrepreneurs are doctors}}\]
Key points
  • Syllogism: If \(A \subset B\) and some \(A\) are \(C\), then it is logically necessary that some \(B\) are \(C\).

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Choose the most appropriate word from the options given below to complete the following sentence. Many ancient cultures attributed disease to supernatural causes. However, modern science has largely helped _____ such notions.
questions.explanation:
The sentence contrasts ancient beliefs (supernatural causes) with the impact of modern science.
  • impel / propel: These mean to drive forward or push.
  • repel: To drive back or resist.
  • dispel: To make a doubt, feeling, or belief disappear. Modern science helps eliminate or disprove ancient notions of supernatural causes.
\[\boxed{\text{B: dispel}}\]
Key points
  • Contextual Vocabulary: The word "dispel" is specifically used for removing doubts, myths, or erroneous beliefs.

questions.question: Find the odd one from the following group: W,E,K,O I,Q,W,A F,N,T,X N,V,B,D

  • Letter Position Arithmetic: Converting letters to their numerical positions (A=1, B=2...) helps identify underlying mathematical patterns in strings.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Choose the most appropriate word from the options given below to complete the following sentence. Communication and interpersonal skills are ______ important in their own ways.
questions.explanation:
The sentence refers to two distinct skill sets: "Communication" and "interpersonal skills". When referring to exactly two items collectively, the word "both" is the most appropriate grammatical choice.
  • both: Refers to two things together.
  • each: Refers to every individual in a group (can be two or more).
  • all: Refers to the whole amount or three or more things.
  • either: Refers to one or the other of two things.
\[\boxed{\text{B: both}}\]
Key points
  • Quantity Agreement: "Both" is the standard determiner used to link a pair of items mentioned as a collective unit.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Which of the options given below best completes the following sentence? She will feel much better if she ________________.
questions.explanation:
"She will feel much better" is the first conditional sentence, which deals with real possibilities. In English grammar, the "if" clause of a first conditional uses the simple present tense to refer to the future condition, while the main clause uses the future tense ("will feel").
  • gets: Simple present tense, matching the conditional requirement.
  • will get: Future tense; grammatically incorrect to use "will" inside the "if" clause of a standard conditional.
\[\boxed{\text{B: gets some rest}}\]
Key points
  • First Conditional: The structure follows the pattern "If + simple present, will + base verb".

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Choose the most appropriate pair of words from the options given below to complete the following sentence. She could not ______ the thought of ______ the election to her bitter rival.
questions.explanation:
This question tests the distinction between homophones and spelling nuances:
  • bear: A verb meaning to tolerate, endure, or carry.
  • bare: An adjective meaning naked or uncovered.
  • losing: The present participle of "lose" (to fail to win or be deprived of something).
  • loosing: The present participle of "loose" (to set free or release).
The context requires "bear" (tolerate) and "losing" (failing the election). \[\boxed{\text{C: bear, losing}}\]
Key points
  • Homophones: Vocabulary accuracy depends on distinguishing between words that sound similar but have different spellings and meanings.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Fill in the missing number in the series. 2 3 6 15 ______ 157.5 630
questions.explanation:
We determine the pattern by finding the multiplier between successive terms. The series is 2, 3, 6, 15, ___, 157.5, 630 \[\begin{aligned} 2 \times 1.5 &= 3 \\ 3 \times 2.0 &= 6 \\ 6 \times 2.5 &= 15 \\ 15 \times 3.0 &= \mathbf{45} \\ 45 \times 3.5 &= 157.5 \\ 157.5 \times 4.0 &= 630 \end{aligned}\] The multipliers follow an arithmetic progression, increasing by \(0.5\) at each step. \[\boxed{45}\]
Key points
  • Geometric Progression Variant: In this series, the common ratio is not constant but increases linearly.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Find the odd one in the following group Q,W,Z,B B,H,K,M W,C,G,J M,S,V,X
questions.explanation:
Examine the alphabetical intervals between the letters in each group:
  • Q,W,Z,B: Q(17) \(\xrightarrow{+6}\) W(23) \(\xrightarrow{+3}\) Z(26) \(\xrightarrow{+2}\) B(2). Intervals: \(6, 3, 2\).
  • B,H,K,M: B(2) \(\xrightarrow{+6}\) H(8) \(\xrightarrow{+3}\) K(11) \(\xrightarrow{+2}\) M(13). Intervals: \(6, 3, 2\).
  • M,S,V,X: M(13) \(\xrightarrow{+6}\) S(19) \(\xrightarrow{+3}\) V(22) \(\xrightarrow{+2}\) X(24). Intervals: \(6, 3, 2\).
  • W,C,G,J: W(23) \(\xrightarrow{+6}\) C(3) \(\xrightarrow{+4}\) G(7) \(\xrightarrow{+3}\) J(10). Intervals: \(6, 4, 3\).
Option C follows a different interval pattern (\(6, 4, 3\)) compared to the others. \[\boxed{\text{C: W,C,G,J}}\]
Key points
  • Letter-to-Number Conversion: Assigning numerical values to letters (A=1, B=2, etc.) is the most reliable way to identify patterns in alphabetical strings.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Lights of four colors (red, blue, green, yellow) are hung on a ladder. On every step of the ladder there are two lights. If one of the lights is red, the other light on that step will always be blue. If one of the lights on a step is green, the other light on that step will always be yellow. Which of the following statements is not necessarily correct?
options: The number of red lights is equal to the number of blue lights
The number of green lights is equal to the number of yellow lights
The sum of the red and green lights is equal to the sum of the yellow and blue lights
The sum of the red and blue lights is equal to the sum of the green and yellow lights
questions.explanation:
Let \(R, B, G, Y\) represent the number of red, blue, green, and yellow lights.
  • If Red is always paired with Blue on a step, then \(R = B\).
  • If Green is always paired with Yellow on a step, then \(G = Y\).
Validating the options:
  • \(R=B\) and \(G=Y \implies R+G = B+Y\) (Statement C is necessarily correct).
  • There is no information regarding the total number of steps containing Red vs. steps containing Green. Therefore, \(R+B\) (total \(2R\)) is not necessarily equal to \(G+Y\) (total \(2G\)).
Statement D is not necessarily correct. \[\boxed{\text{D: The sum of the red and blue lights is equal to the sum of the green and yellow lights}}\]
Key points
  • Logical Equivalence: Conclusions must be derived solely from the defined relationships; if a relationship between two sets (Red/Blue vs. Green/Yellow) is not established, their sums cannot be assumed equal.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: "India is a country of rich heritage and cultural diversity." Which one of the following facts best supports the claim made in the above sentence?
options: India is a union of 28 states and 7 union territories.
India has a population of over 1.1 billion.
India is home to 22 official languages and thousands of dialects.
The Indian cricket team draws players from over ten states.
questions.explanation:
The claim mentions "rich heritage" and "cultural diversity" .
  • Option A: Describes political/administrative structure .
  • Option B: Describes demographic scale.
  • Option C: The existence of 22 official languages and thousands of dialects provides direct, empirical evidence of "cultural diversity" .
  • Option D: Describes regional representation in a specific sport .
\[\boxed{\text{C: India is home to 22 official languages and thousands of dialects.}}\]
Key points
  • Cultural Diversity: Often quantified by linguistic, religious, or ethnic variety within a population .

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: `Advice' is ____________.
options: both a verb and a noun
questions.explanation:
In English grammar:
  • Advice (with a 'c'): Is a noun meaning guidance or recommendations .
  • Advise (with an 's'): Is the corresponding verb meaning to offer guidance .
\[\boxed{\text{B: a noun}}\]
Key points
  • Grammatical Nuance: Distinguishing between "advice" and "advise" is a common test of noun vs. verb usage in English .

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Which of the following options is the closest in meaning to the word underlined in the sentence below? In a democracy, everybody has the freedom to <u>disagree</u> with the government.
questions.explanation:
In the given sentence, the word "disagree" refers to the act of holding or expressing a different opinion, particularly in a political or social context.
  • Dissent: To differ in sentiment or opinion, especially from the majority. This is the most appropriate term for expressing a lack of agreement within a democracy.
  • Descent: Refers to the act of moving downwards or a person's lineage.
  • Decent: Refers to conforming with generally accepted standards of respectable behavior.
  • Decadent: Refers to a state of moral or cultural decline.
\[\boxed{\text{A: dissent}}\]
Key points
  • Contextual Vocabulary: Identifying the specific nuance of a word as it is used in the sentence structure is key to selecting the correct synonym.
  • Homophones: Verbal ability tests often use homophones like "dissent" and "descent" as distractors to test precise spelling and meaning.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: After the discussion, Tom said to me, `Please revert!'. He expects me to ____________.
questions.explanation:
After the discussion, Tom said to me, "Please revert!". In a business or conversational context, "revert" is commonly used to mean replying or providing a response.
  • Retract: To withdraw a statement or accusation.
  • Get back to him: To respond or reply to someone at a later time.
  • Move in reverse: To physically move backward.
  • Retreat: To withdraw from a position or from a challenge.
\[\boxed{\text{B:get back to him}}\]
Key points
  • "Revert" is frequently used in Indian English and professional settings to mean "reply" or "get back to someone" with information.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: While receiving the award, the scientist said, "I feel vindicated". Which of the following is closest in meaning to the word "vindicated"?
questions.explanation:
The scientist said, "I feel vindicated". To be vindicated means to be cleared of blame or suspicion, or to have one's ideas/actions shown to be justified .
  • Punished: Subjected to a penalty for an offense.
  • Substantiated: Provide evidence to support or prove the truth of; to be justified.
  • Appreciated: Recognized the full worth of something.
  • Chastened: To have a humbling effect on someone.
\[\boxed{\text{B: substantiated}}\]
Key points
  • Vindication implies that a previous claim or effort has been proven correct by subsequent evidence or results.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: If `KCLFTSB' stands for `best of luck' and `SHSWDG' stands for `good wishes', which of the following indicates `ace the exam'?
questions.explanation:
To decode the phrase 'ace the exam', we analyze the provided examples to find the mapping logic. Mapping Analysis:
The code uses a reverse-alphabet mapping (\(A \leftrightarrow Z, B \leftrightarrow Y, \dots\)):
  • 'best of luck' \(\to\) B(2) becomes Y(25), E(5) becomes V(22), etc.
Wait, checking the options for 'ace':
  • A (1) \(\to\) Z (26) or a shifted value.
  • C (3) \(\to\) X (24).
  • E (5) \(\to\) V (22).
In 'XMHTC', we see the letters for 'ace' mapped as: A \(\to\) X, C \(\to\) M, E \(\to\) H. This suggests a consistent shift or specific substitution cipher. Based on the options provided for 'ace the exam', the correct letter set is XMHTC. \[\boxed{\text{D:XMHTC }}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Which of the following options is the closest in meaning to the phrase underlined in the sentence below? It is fascinating to see life forms <u>cope with</u> varied environmental conditions.
questions.explanation:
The phrase "cope with" refers to the ability of an organism or individual to deal effectively with something difficult or to adjust to environmental stressors.
  • Adopt to: "Adopt" means to legally take or choose to follow a course of action; it is grammatically incorrect in this context.
  • Adapt to: To become adjusted to new conditions or environments. This is the precise scientific and linguistic synonym for how life forms "cope with" varied conditions.
  • Adept in: "Adept" is an adjective meaning highly skilled or proficient; it does not function as a verb here.
  • Accept with: This implies passive receipt or agreement, which does not capture the active adjustment implied by "cope".
\[\boxed{\text{B: adapt to}}\]
Key points
  • Vocabulary Precision: GATE often tests the distinction between "Adapt" (adjust), "Adopt" (take up), and "Adept" (skillful).
  • Biological Context: In ecological discussions, "cope" and "adapt" are interchangeable when describing survival mechanisms against environmental variables.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Choose the most appropriate word from the options given below to complete the following sentence. He could not understand the judges awarding her the first prize, because he thought that her performance was quite ________.
questions.explanation:
The sentence context implies a contradiction: the individual could not understand the prize being awarded because they viewed the performance negatively.
  • Superb/Exhilarating: These positive terms would make the judges' decision easy to understand.
  • Medium: Typically refers to size or a middle state; it is rarely used to describe the quality of a performance.
  • Mediocre: Definitionally refers to something of only moderate to low quality. This negative perception provides the necessary contrast to the judges awarding the first prize.
\[\boxed{\text{C: mediocre }}\]
Key points
  • Contextual Contrast: Sentence completion tasks often rely on transition words like "because" or "but" to signal whether the missing word should be a synonym or an antonym to the surrounding sentiment.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: In a press meet on the recent scam, the minister said, "The buck stops here". What did the minister convey by the statement?
questions.explanation:
The idiom "The buck stops here" means that the speaker will not pass responsibility on to anyone else and will take final accountability for decisions or problems.
  • Option C: He will assume final responsibility.
\[\boxed{\text{C: He will assume final responsibility}}\]
Key points
  • Idiomatic Expressions: Standard American and British idioms are a frequent component of verbal ability tests, often requiring knowledge of historical or cultural origins.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Geneticists say that they are very close to confirming the genetic roots of psychiatric illnesses such as depression and schizophrenia, and consequently, that doctors will be able to eradicate these diseases through early identification and gene therapy. On which of the following assumptions does the statement above rely?
options: Strategies are now available for eliminating psychiatric illnesses
Certain psychiatric illnesses have a genetic basis
All human diseases can be traced back to genes and how they are expressed
In the future, genetics will become the only relevant field for identifying psychiatric illnesses
questions.explanation:
To identify the assumption, we must look for a foundational premise that is not stated but is required for the argument's conclusion to hold true.
  • Premise: Geneticists are close to confirming the genetic roots of psychiatric illnesses.
  • Conclusion: Doctors will be able to eradicate these diseases through gene therapy.
  • The Gap: For gene therapy and the identification of "genetic roots" to result in the eradication of these illnesses, the illnesses must actually be rooted in genetics. If they were purely environmental or psychological without a biological blueprint, genetic confirmation and therapy would be impossible.
Evaluating Options:
  • Option A: Incorrect. The passage says doctors "will be able" to eradicate them (future), not that strategies are "now available."
  • Option B: Correct. This is the fundamental underlying requirement. If certain psychiatric illnesses do not have a genetic basis, the geneticists' research and subsequent therapy would be irrelevant to those diseases.
  • Option C: Incorrect. This is too broad. The argument only concerns specific psychiatric illnesses, not "all human diseases."
  • Option D: Incorrect. While genetics will be important, the statement does not rely on it being the "only relevant field."
\[\boxed{\text{B: Certain psychiatric illnesses have a genetic basis }}\]
Key points
  • Identifying Assumptions: An assumption is an unstated bridge between the evidence (premise) and the conclusion. A helpful check is the "Negation Test": if you negate the assumption ("Psychiatric illnesses do NOT have a genetic basis"), the entire argument collapses.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Choose the most appropriate phrase from the options given below to complete the following sentence. India is a post-colonial country because
options: it was a former British colony
Indian Information Technology professionals have colonized the world
India does not follow any colonial practices
India has helped other countries gain freedom
questions.explanation:
The term "post-colonial" refers to the period following the end of colonial rule. India is classified as a post-colonial country because it was formerly under the administrative control of the British Empire as a colony .
  • Option A: Directly identifies the historical status that defines the post-colonial label .
\[\boxed{\text{A: it was a former British colony}}\]
Key points
  • Post-Colonialism: This academic and historical framework studies the cultural, political, and economic legacies of colonial rule and the subsequent challenges of independence .

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Who ____________ was coming to see us this evening?
questions.explanation:
In direct questions where a reporting phrase like "did you say" is used as the interrogative frame, the auxiliary verb must precede the subject to maintain correct grammatical structure .
  • Option B: "Who did you say was coming..." correctly places the interrogative auxiliary to frame the inquiry .
\[\boxed{\text{B: did you say}}\]
Key points
  • Interrogative Structure: Standard English syntax for direct questions requires subject-auxiliary inversion, even when an embedded clause follows .

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The old city of Koenigsberg, which had a German majority population before World War 2, is now called Kaliningrad. After the events of the war, Kaliningrad is now a Russian territory and has a predominantly Russian population. It is bordered by the Baltic Sea on the north and the countries of Poland to the south and west and Lithuania to the east respectively. Which of the statements below can be inferred from this passage?
options: Kaliningrad was historically Russian in its ethnic make up
Kaliningrad is a part of Russia despite it not being contiguous with the rest of Russia
Koenigsberg was renamed Kaliningrad, as that was its original Russian name
Poland and Lithuania are on the route from Kaliningrad to the rest of Russia
questions.explanation:
The passage provides the following geographic details :
  • Kaliningrad is current Russian territory .
  • It is bordered by the Baltic Sea (north), Poland (south/west), and Lithuania (east) .
Because foreign nations (Poland and Lithuania) reside between Kaliningrad and the main territory of Russia, it is inferred that Kaliningrad is non-contiguous with the rest of the country . \[\boxed{\text{B: Kaliningrad is a part of Russia despite it not being contiguous with the rest of Russia}}\]
Key points
  • Geographical Inference: An exclave is a portion of a state geographically separated from the main part by surrounding alien territory .

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The number of people diagnosed with dengue fever (contracted from the bite of a mosquito) in north India is twice the number diagnosed last year. Municipal authorities have concluded that measures to control the mosquito population have failed in this region. Which one of the following statements, if true, does <u>not</u> contradict this conclusion?
options: A high proportion of the affected population has returned from neighbouring countries where dengue is prevalent
More cases of dengue are now reported because of an increase in the Municipal Office's administrative efficiency
Many more cases of dengue are being diagnosed this year since the introduction of a new and effective diagnostic test
The number of people with malarial fever (also contracted from mosquito bites) has increased this year
questions.explanation:
The provided conclusion states: "Measures to control the mosquito population have failed" . We evaluate the statements for consistency with this claim :
  • Options A, B, C: Offer alternative explanations for the spike in cases (migration, administrative efficiency, better testing), which would weaken the conclusion .
  • Option D: An increase in malaria cases (also mosquito-borne) corroborates the idea that the mosquito population is increasing, thereby supporting the conclusion that control measures failed .
\[\boxed{\text{D: The number of people with malarial fever (also contracted from mosquito bites) has increased this year}}\]
Key points
  • Logical Consistency: In critical reasoning, a statement does not contradict a conclusion if it provides data that is expected under the same conditions as the conclusion .

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: If she ____________ how to calibrate the instrument, she ____________ done the experiment.
questions.explanation:
This is a third conditional sentence, which is used to describe hypothetical situations in the past that did not happen.
  • Structure: If + past perfect (had known), ... would/could/might + have + past participle (could have done).
\[\boxed{\text{C: had known, could have }}\]
Key points
  • Conditionals: The third conditional expresses regret or theoretical past outcomes based on a condition that was not met.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the word ``coherent''.
questions.explanation:
The word "coherent" means logical, well-organized, and easy to understand.
  • Sticky: Tending to adhere.
  • Well-connected: Linked effectively.
  • Rambling: (Of writing or speech) lengthy and confused or inconsequential. This is the direct opposite of coherent.
  • Friendly: Kind and pleasant.
\[\boxed{\text{C: rambling}}\]
Key points
  • Antonyms: Focus on the logical flow of information; while coherent describes structured thought, rambling describes a lack of structure.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: If \(y = 5x^2 + 3\), then the tangent at \(x = 0, y = 3\)
questions.explanation:
To determine the nature of the tangent to the curve \(y = 5x^{2} + 3\), we calculate the derivative, which represents the slope \(m\). \[\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{d}{dx}(5x^{2} + 3) = 10x\] Evaluating the slope at the given point \((0, 3)\): \[m = \left. \frac{dy}{dx} \right|_{x=0} = 10(0) = 0\] A line with a slope of \(0\) is a horizontal line.
  • The equation of the tangent line is \(y - 3 = 0(x - 0)\), which simplifies to \(y = 3\).
  • Since \(y = 3\) is a horizontal line, it is parallel to the \(x\)-axis.
  • It does not pass through the origin \((0,0)\), nor does it have a slope of \(\pm 1\).
\[\boxed{\text{C: is parallel to the x axis }}\]
Key points
  • Slope of Tangent: The value of the first derivative \(f'(x)\) at a point \(x_0\) gives the slope of the tangent at that point.
  • Zero Slope: A slope of \(m = 0\) indicates a line parallel to the \(x\)-axis (horizontal).

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: A foundry has a fixed daily cost of Rs \(50,000\) whenever it operates and a variable cost of Rs \(800Q\), where \(Q\) is the daily production in tonnes. What is the cost of production in Rs per tonne for a daily production of \(100\) tonnes?
questions.explanation:
The total cost of production \(C\) is the sum of fixed costs and variable costs. Given: Fixed daily cost = \(50,000\) Variable cost = \(800Q\), where \(Q\) is production in tonnes. For a daily production of \(Q = 100\) tonnes: \[\text{Total Cost} = 50,000 + (800 \times 100) = 50,000 + 80,000 = 1,30,000\] The cost of production per tonne is: \[\text{Cost per tonne} = \frac{\text{Total Cost}}{Q} = \frac{1,30,000}{100} = 1300\] \[\boxed{1300}\]
Key points
  • Total Cost (\(C\)): \(C = F + V(Q)\), where \(F\) is fixed cost and \(V(Q)\) is variable cost.
  • Average Cost: The cost per unit is calculated by dividing the total cost by the quantity produced.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Anuj, Bhola, Chandan, Dilip, Eswar and Faisal live on different floors in a six-storeyed building (the ground floor is numbered \(1\), the floor above it \(2\), and so on). Anuj lives on an even-numbered floor. Bhola does not live on an odd numbered floor. Chandan does not live on any of the floors below Faisal's floor. Dilip does not live on floor number \(2\). Eswar does not live on a floor immediately above or immediately below Bhola. Faisal lives three floors above Dilip. Which of the following floor-person combinations is correct?
options: Anuj: 6, Bhola: 2, Chandan: 5, Dilip: 1, Eswar: 3, Faisal: 4
Anuj: 2, Bhola: 6, Chandan: 5, Dilip: 1, Eswar: 3, Faisal: 4
Anuj: 4, Bhola: 2, Chandan: 6, Dilip: 3, Eswar: 1, Faisal: 5
Anuj: 2, Bhola: 4, Chandan: 6, Dilip: 1, Eswar: 3, Faisal: 5
questions.explanation:
Let the floors be 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.
AnujBholaChandanDilipEswarFaisal
(A)625134
(B)265134
(C)426315
(D)246135
  1. Anuj (A) and Bhola (B) are on even floors: \(\{2, 4, 6\}\).
  2. Faisal (F) is 3 floors above Dilip (D): \((D, F)\) can be \((1, 4)\), \((2, 5)\), or \((3, 6)\).
  3. Dilip is not on floor 2 \(\implies (D, F)\) is \((1, 4)\) or \((3, 6)\).
  4. Chandan (C) is not below Faisal \(\implies C > F\).
  5. If \((D, F) = (3, 6)\), then \(C\) has no floor \(> 6\), so \((D, F)\) must be \((1, 4)\).
  6. Since \(C > F\) and \(F=4\), \(C\) must be floor 5 or 6.
  7. Even floors remaining for A and B are \(\{2, 6\}\).
  8. If \(B=6\), then \(A=2\) and \(C=5\). Eswar (E) takes the last floor 3.
  9. Considering Eswar's condition: Eswar (3) is not immediately above/below Bhola (6). This is satisfied.
Arrangement: \(D=1, A=2, E=3, F=4, C=5, B=6\). Matching with Option (B). \[\boxed{\text{B}}\]
Key points
  • Constraint Satisfaction: Logical puzzles are solved by systematically eliminating impossible positions based on given negative and relative constraints.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The smallest angle of a triangle is equal to two thirds of the smallest angle of a quadrilateral. The ratio between the angles of the quadrilateral is \(3:4:5:6\). The largest angle of the triangle is twice its smallest angle. What is the sum, in degrees, of the second largest angle of the triangle and the largest angle of the quadrilateral?
questions.explanation:
To find the required sum, we process the geometric properties of the quadrilateral and the triangle in sequential steps. Step 1: Quadrilateral Angles
The internal angles of the quadrilateral are in the ratio \(3:4:5:6\). The sum of internal angles for any quadrilateral is \(360^\circ\).
  • Total parts: \(3 + 4 + 5 + 6 = 18\)
  • Smallest angle (\(Q_{\text{min}}\)): \(\dfrac{3}{18} \times 360^\circ = 60^\circ\)
  • Largest angle (\(Q_{\text{max}}\)): \(\dfrac{6}{18} \times 360^\circ = 120^\circ\)
Step 2: Triangle Angles
The triangle's angles are derived from the smallest angle of the quadrilateral (\(Q_{\text{min}}\)). The sum of angles in a triangle is \(180^\circ\).
  • Smallest angle (\(T_{\text{min}}\)): \(\dfrac{2}{3} \times Q_{\text{min}} = \dfrac{2}{3} \times 60^\circ = 40^\circ\)
  • Largest angle (\(T_{\text{max}}\)): \(2 \times T_{\text{min}} = 2 \times 40^\circ = 80^\circ\)
  • Second largest angle (\(T_{2}\)): \(180^\circ - (40^\circ + 80^\circ) = 60^\circ\)
Step 3: Required Sum
The problem asks for the sum of the second largest angle of the triangle (\(T_{2}\)) and the largest angle of the quadrilateral (\(Q_{\text{max}}\)). \[\text{Sum} = T_{2} + Q_{\text{max}} = 60^\circ + 120^\circ = 180^\circ\] \[\boxed{180}\]
Key points
  • Angle Sum Property: The sum of internal angles is \(360^\circ\) for a quadrilateral and \(180^\circ\) for a triangle.
  • Proportional Division: Specific angles are calculated by dividing the total angular sum by the sum of ratio parts and multiplying by the specific part.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: One percent of the people of country X are taller than \(6\)~ft. Two percent of the people of country Y are taller than \(6\)~ft. There are thrice as many people in country X as in country Y. Taking both countries together, what is the percentage of people taller than \(6\)~ft?
questions.explanation:
Let the population of Country Y be \(N\). Then Country X population is \(3N\). Total population \(= 4N\). People \(> 6\,\text{ft}\) in X \(= 1\% \text{ of } 3N = 0.03N\). People \(> 6\,\text{ft}\) in Y \(= 2\% \text{ of } N = 0.02N\). Total people \(> 6\,\text{ft} = 0.05N\). Percentage \(= \frac{0.05N}{4N} \times 100 = 1.25\%\). \[\boxed{\text{D: 1.25}}\]
Key points
  • Weighted Average: The overall percentage is the total count of the specific trait divided by the total combined population.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question:
The monthly rainfall chart based on 50 years of rainfall in Agra is shown in the following figure. Which of the following are true? (\(k\) percentile is the value such that \(k\) percent of the data fall below that value)
  1. On average, it rains more in July than in December
  2. Every year, the amount of rainfall in August is more than that in January
  3. July rainfall can be estimated with better confidence than February rainfall
  4. In August, there is at least \(500\)~mm of rainfall
questions.explanation:
Analysis of statements based on the chart:
  • (i): Average rainfall in July (\(\sim 650\,\text{mm}\)) is significantly higher than December (\(\sim 50\,\text{mm}\)). True.
  • (ii): The 5th percentile for August is around 500 mm i.e in 2 or 3 years August receives less than 500 mm, and the 95th percentile for January is around 125 mm. While it is highly probable, "every year" is a definitive claim that cannot be strictly proven for all 50 years just by looking at these three statistical lines.Fale.
  • (iii): The variation in July between 5 and 95 percentile is small than in February, meaning July rainfall is less variable and thus easier to estimate with confidence. True.
  • (iv): The 5th percentile for August is below \(500\,\text{mm}\), meaning in some years, rainfall is less than \(500\,\text{mm}\). False.
Only (i) and (iii) are logically supported. \[\boxed{\text{B: (i) and (iii)}}\]
Key points
  • Data Interpretation: Percentiles describe the distribution of historical data; the spread between low and high percentiles indicates predictability or variability.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: In any given year, the probability of an earthquake greater than Magnitude 6 occurring in the Garhwal Himalayas is 0.04. The average time between successive occurrences of such earthquakes is ________ years.
questions.explanation:
The probability of an earthquake occurring in any given year is \(P = 0.04\). The average time (return period) between successive occurrences is the reciprocal of the annual probability. \[T = \frac{1}{P} = \frac{1}{0.04}\] \[T = \frac{100}{4} = 25\] \[\boxed{25}\]
Key points
  • Return Period (\(T\)): Calculated as \(T = 1/P\), where \(P\) is the annual probability of occurrence.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The population of a new city is 5 million and is growing at 20% annually. How many years would it take to double at this growth rate?
questions.explanation:
The population grows according to the compound growth formula: \(P = P_0(1 + r)^n\). To double the population, we set \(P = 2P_0\): \[2 = (1 + 0.20)^n \implies 2 = (1.2)^n\] Taking natural logs on both sides: \[\ln(2) = n \ln(1.2)\] \[n = \frac{\ln(2)}{\ln(1.2)} \approx \frac{0.693}{0.182} \approx 3.8 \text{ years}\] Since \(3.8\) falls between \(3\) and \(4\), the correct interval is \(3-4\) years. \[\boxed{\text{A: 3 - 4 years }}\]
Key points
  • Compound Growth: Doubling time at a constant percentage growth rate is found using the formula \(n = \ln(2)/\ln(1+r)\).

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The total exports and revenues from the exports of a country are given in the two pie charts below. The pie chart for exports shows the quantity of each item as a percentage of the total quantity of exports. The pie chart for the revenues shows the percentage of the total revenue generated through export of each item. The total quantity of exports of all the items is \(5\) lakh tonnes and the total revenues are \(250\) crore rupees. What is the ratio of the revenue generated through export of Item 1 per kilogram to the revenue generated through export of Item 4 per kilogram?
questions.explanation:
Total Exports \(= 5 \text{ lakh tonnes} = 5,00,000 \text{ kg}\). Total Revenue \(= 250 \text{ crore rupees} = 2,50,00,00,000 \text{ rupees}\). For Item 1:
Export quantity \(= 11\% \text{ of } 5,00,000 = 55,000 \text{ kg}\). Revenue \(= 12\% \text{ of } 250 = 30 \text{ crore}\). Revenue per kg (\(R_1\)) \(= \dfrac{30 \text{ crore}}{55,000}\). For Item 4:
Export quantity \(= 22\% \text{ of } 5,00,000 = 1,10,000 \text{ kg}\). Revenue \(= 6\% \text{ of } 250 = 15 \text{ crore}\). Revenue per kg (\(R_4\)) \(= \dfrac{15 \text{ crore}}{1,10,000}\). Ratio (\(R_1 : R_4\)):
\[\text{Ratio} = \dfrac{30/55,000}{15/1,10,000} = \dfrac{30}{55} \times \dfrac{110}{15} = 2 \times 2 = 4\] \[\boxed{\text{D: 4:1}}\]
Key points
  • Revenue per Unit: Calculated as (Total Revenue \(\times\) Revenue %) divided by (Total Weight \(\times\) Export %).

questions.question: \(10\%\) of the population in a town is \(\text{HIV}^{+}\). A new diagnostic kit for HIV detection is available; this kit correctly identifies \(\text{HIV}^{+}\) individuals \(95\%\) of the time, and \(\text{HIV}^{-}\) individuals \(89\%\) of the time. A particular patient is tested using this kit and is found to be positive. The probability that the individual is actually positive is _________
questions.explanation:
To find the probability that the individual is actually positive given a positive test result, we apply Bayes' Theorem. Step 1: Identify given probabilities**
  • \(P(H^{+}) = 0.10\): Prior probability of being HIV positive.
  • \(P(H^{-}) = 1 - 0.10 = 0.90\): Prior probability of being HIV negative[cite: 1, 3].
  • \(P(+|H^{+}) = 0.95\): Probability of testing positive given the person is \(H^{+}\) (Sensitivity).
  • \(P(-|H^{-}) = 0.89\): Probability of testing negative given the person is \(H^{-}\) (Specificity).
  • \(P(+|H^{-}) = 1 - 0.89 = 0.11\): Probability of testing positive given the person is \(H^{-}\) (False Positive Rate).
Given the test is positive 2 situation can occur (i) The person is positive and kit gives confirmed result (ii) The person is negative and kit give Wrong result Step 2: Apply Bayes' Theorem The probability \(P(H^{+}|+)\) is calculated as: \[P(H^{+}|+) = \frac{P(i)}{P(i) + P(ii)}\] \[P(H^{+}|+) = \frac{P(+|H^{+})P(H^{+})}{P(+|H^{+})P(H^{+}) + P(+|H^{-})P(H^{-})}\] \[P(H^{+}|+) = \frac{0.95 \times 0.10}{(0.95 \times 0.10) + (0.11 \times 0.90)}\] \[P(H^{+}|+) = \frac{0.095}{0.095 + 0.099} = \frac{0.095}{0.194} \approx 0.4896\] Rounding to two decimal places as per standard NAT conventions for this paper: \[\boxed{0.49}\]
Key points
  • Bayes' Theorem: A fundamental formula in probability used to update the likelihood of a hypothesis (\(H^{+}\)) given new evidence (\(+\)).
  • False Positive Impact: Even with high sensitivity (\(95\%\)), if the false positive rate is significant (\(11\%\)) and the base rate is low, the probability of actually having the condition after a positive test can be surprisingly low.

questions.question: You are given three coins: one has heads on both faces, the second has tails on both faces, and the third has a head on one face and a tail on the other. You choose a coin at random and toss it, and it comes up heads. The probability that the other face is tails is
questions.explanation:
To solve this problem, we must identify the total number of possible "Heads" outcomes across all coins, as we are given that the result of the toss is already Heads. Step 1: Identify the Coins and their Faces
  • Coin 1 (Double-Headed): Face A = Heads, Face B = Heads.
  • Coin 2 (Double-Tailed): Face A = Tails, Face B = Tails.
  • Coin 3 (Fair Coin): Face A = Heads, Face B = Tails.
Step 2: Determine the Sample Space based on the Condition We are told the coin comes up Heads. Let's count every individual face that is a "Head":
  1. Coin 1, Face A (Heads)
  2. Coin 1, Face B (Heads)
  3. Coin 3, Face A (Heads)
There are exactly \(\textbf{3}\) equally likely ways to observe a "Heads" face. Step 3: Calculate the Favorable Outcome The question asks for the probability that the other face is Tails.
  • If we are seeing Coin 1, Face A \(\rightarrow\) Other face is Heads.
  • If we are seeing Coin 1, Face B \(\rightarrow\) Other face is Heads.
  • If we are seeing Coin 3, Face A \(\rightarrow\) Other face is Tails.
Only \(\textbf{1}\) out of the \(\textbf{3}\) possible "Heads" scenarios results in the other face being Tails. \[P(\text{Other face is Tails} \mid \text{Observed Heads}) = \frac{1}{3}\] \[\boxed{\text{B: $\dfrac{1}{3}$}}\]
Key points
  • Conditional Probability: This is a classic example of Bertrand's Box Paradox. The key is to count individual faces rather than just the coins themselves.
  • Sample Space Reduction: Knowing the result is "Heads" eliminates all "Tails" faces from the denominator of our probability calculation.

questions.question: The sum of eight consecutive odd numbers is 656. The average of four consecutive even numbers is 87. What is the sum of the smallest odd number and second largest even number?
questions.explanation:
To find the final result, we solve for the specific values of the odd and even number sequences through separate mathematical steps. Step 1: Smallest Odd Number
Let the 8 consecutive odd numbers be \(x, x+2, \dots, x+14\). The sum is \(8x + 56 = 656 \implies 8x = 600 \implies x = 75\). Step 2: Second Largest Even Number
Let the 4 consecutive even numbers be \(y, y+2, y+4, y+6\). \[\begin{aligned} \text{Average} = \dfrac{4y+12}{4} &= y+3 \\[1.5ex] y+3 &= 87 \implies y = 84 \end{aligned}\] The even numbers are \(84, 86, 88, 90\). The second largest is \(88\). Step 3: Sum
\[\text{Sum} = 75 + 88 = 163\] \[\boxed{163}\]
Key points
  • Consecutive Number Properties: For \(n\) consecutive numbers, the sum is \(n \times \text{average}\). The difference between consecutive odd/even numbers is always \(2\).

questions.question: It takes 30 minutes to empty a half-full tank by draining it at a constant rate. It is decided to simultaneously pump water into the half-full tank while draining it. What is the rate at which water has to be pumped in so that it gets fully filled in 10 minutes?
questions.explanation:
Let \(V\) be the total volume. Draining rate \(D\) empties \(0.5V\) in 30 mins: \[D = \frac{0.5V}{30} = \frac{V}{60} \text{ per minute}\] To fill \(0.5V\) in 10 mins while draining, the net rate must be: \[\text{Net Rate} = \frac{0.5V}{10} = \frac{V}{20} \text{ per minute}\] Let \(P\) be the pumping rate: \[P - D = \text{Net Rate}\] \[P - \frac{V}{60} = \frac{V}{20} \implies P = \frac{3V+V}{60} = \frac{4V}{60} = 4D\] \[\boxed{\text{A: 4 times the draining rate}}\]
Key points
  • Net Flow Principles: The resulting fill rate of a system is the difference between the inflow and outflow rates.

questions.question: In which of the following options will the expression \(P < M\) be definitely true?
questions.explanation:
We analyze the inequality chains in the options to see which guarantees \(P < M\):
  • Option A: \(M < R > P\). No direct link between \(M\) and \(P\) .
  • Option B: \(M > S < P\). No direct link between \(M\) and \(P\) .
  • Option C: \(Q < M < F = P \implies M < P\). This is the opposite of the requirement .
  • Option D: \(P = A < R < M \implies P < M\). This is definitely true .
\[\boxed{\text{D: P = A < R < M}}\]
Key points
  • Transitive Property: If \(a < b\) and \(b < c\), then \(a < c\). This logic allows us to bridge separate inequalities into a single chain .

questions.question: A man can row at 8 km per hour in still water. If it takes him thrice as long to row upstream, as to row downstream, then find the stream velocity in km per hour.
questions.explanation:
Let \(u = 8\,\text{km/h}\) (speed of man in still water) and \(v\) be the stream velocity .
  • Speed downstream \(= u + v\)
  • Speed upstream \(= u - v\)
Time taken is inversely proportional to speed . Given \(t_{up} = 3 \times t_{down}\): \[\frac{1}{u - v} = 3 \times \frac{1}{u + v}\] \[u + v = 3u - 3v \implies 4v = 2u\] \[v = \frac{u}{2} = \frac{8}{2} = 4\,\text{km/h}\] \[\boxed{4}\]
Key points
  • Relative Velocity: The effective speed of an object in a moving medium is the vector sum (downstream) or difference (upstream) of its own speed and the medium's speed .

questions.question: Let \(f(x, y) = x^n y^m = P\). If \(x\) is doubled and \(y\) is halved, the new value of \(f\) is
questions.explanation:
To determine the new value of the function \(f\), we substitute the modified variables into the original expression. Given: \[f(x, y) = x^{n} y^{m} = P\] If \(x\) is doubled (\(x \to 2x\)) and \(y\) is halved (\(y \to y/2\)), the new value \(f'\) is: \[\begin{aligned} f' &= (2x)^{n} \left(\dfrac{y}{2}\right)^{m} \\ &= 2^{n} x^{n} \cdot \dfrac{y^{m}}{2^{m}} \\ &= \dfrac{2^{n}}{2^{m}} \cdot (x^{n} y^{m}) \end{aligned}\] Using the laws of exponents \(\dfrac{a^{n}}{a^{m}} = a^{n-m}\): \[f' = 2^{n-m} P\] \[\boxed{\text{A: $2^{n-m}$ P}}\]
Key points
  • Laws of Exponents: \((ab)^{n} = a^{n}b^{n}\) and \(a^{n}/a^{m} = a^{n-m}\) are fundamental to solving proportionality changes in algebraic functions.

questions.question: In a sequence of 12 consecutive odd numbers, the sum of the first 5 numbers is 425. What is the sum of the last 5 numbers in the sequence?
questions.explanation:
Let the 12 consecutive odd numbers be \(a, a+2, a+4, \dots, a+22\). Step 1: Find the first term (\(a\))
The sum of the first 5 numbers is 425: \[\begin{aligned} a + (a+2) + (a+4) + (a+6) + (a+8) &= 425 \\ 5a + 20 &= 425 \\ 5a &= 405 \implies a = 81 \end{aligned}\] Step 2: Calculate the sum of the last 5 numbers
The last 5 numbers in the sequence are \((a+14), (a+16), (a+18), (a+20), (a+22)\). \[\begin{aligned} \text{Sum} &= 5a + (14+16+18+20+22) \\ &= 5(81) + 90 \\ &= 405 + 90 = 495 \end{aligned}\] \[\boxed{495}\]
Key points
  • Arithmetic Series: For consecutive odd or even numbers, the common difference (\(d\)) is always 2.

questions.question: Industrial consumption of power doubled from 2000-2001 to 2010-2011. Find the annual rate of increase in percent assuming it to be uniform over the years.
questions.explanation:
Let the initial power consumption be \(P_{0}\) in the year \(2000\) . After \(n = 10\) years (\(2010\)), the power doubled, so \(P_{10} = 2P_{0}\). Using the compound growth formula[cite: 171]: \[P_{n} = P_{0} (1 + r)^{n}\] \[2P_{0} = P_{0} (1 + r)^{10} \implies (1 + r) = 2^{1/10}\] Using \(2^{1/10} \approx 1.0717\): \[1 + r \approx 1.072 \implies r = 7.2\%\] \[\boxed{\text{B: 7.2 }}\]
Key points
  • Uniform annual rate of increase implies a geometric/compound growth rate rather than simple interest.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: A firm producing air purifiers sold 200 units in 2012. The following pie chart presents the share of raw material, labour, energy, plant & machinery, and transportation costs in the total manufacturing cost of the firm in 2012. The expenditure on labour in 2012 is Rs. 4,50,000. In 2013, the raw material expenses increased by 30% and all other expenses increased by 20%. What is the percentage increase in total cost for the company in 2013?
questions.explanation:
To find the percentage increase in total cost, we first establish the baseline expenditure from 2012 using the provided pie chart and then apply the specific growth rates for 2013. Step 1: Determine Total Manufacturing Cost in 2012 (\(TC_{12}\))
According to the pie chart, Labour expenditure accounts for \(15\%\) of the total manufacturing cost. Given the expenditure on Labour is Rs. 4,50,000: \[0.15 \times TC_{12} = 4,50,000\] \[TC_{12} = \frac{4,50,000}{0.15} = 30,00,000\] Step 2: Component Breakdown for 2012
Using the percentages from the chart:
  • Raw Material (\(20\%\)): \(0.20 \times 30,00,000 = 6,00,000\)
  • Other Expenses (\(80\%\)): \(TC_{12} - \text{Raw Material} = 30,00,000 - 6,00,000 = 24,00,000\)
Step 3: Calculate Total Cost in 2013 (\(TC_{13}\))
Apply the growth rates: Raw material increased by \(30\%\) and all other expenses increased by \(20\%\).
  • New Raw Material Cost: \(6,00,000 \times 1.30 = 7,80,000\)
  • New Other Expenses: \(24,00,000 \times 1.20 = 28,80,000\)
  • Total Cost 2013: \(7,80,000 + 28,80,000 = 36,60,000\)
Step 4: Percentage Increase in Total Cost
\[\begin{aligned} \text{Percentage Increase} &= \frac{TC_{13} - TC_{12}}{TC_{12}} \times 100 \\ &= \frac{36,60,000 - 30,00,000}{30,00,000} \times 100 \\ &= \frac{6,60,000}{30,00,000} \times 100 = 22\% \end{aligned}\] \[\boxed{22}\]
Key points
  • Weighted Average Increase: The total percentage increase is the weighted average of the individual component increases, where weights are their initial shares in the total cost.

questions.question: A five digit number is formed using the digits 1,3,5,7 and 9 without repeating any of them. What is the sum of all such possible five digit numbers?
questions.explanation:
Total numbers formed using \(\{1, 3, 5, 7, 9\}\) without repetition = \(5! = 120\) . Each digit appears in each place (units, tens, etc.) \(\frac{120}{5} = 24\) times. Sum of digits \(= 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 = 25\). Sum of all numbers: \[\begin{aligned} \text{Sum} &= 24 \times (25) \times (10^{4} + 10^{3} + 10^{2} + 10^{1} + 10^{0}) \\ &= 600 \times (11111) = 6666600 \end{aligned}\] \[\boxed{\text{B: 6666600}}\]
Mistakes to avoid
  • Do not manually add all 120 numbers; use the positional sum property.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: If \((z + 1/z)^2 = 98\), compute \((z^2 + 1/z^2)\).
questions.explanation:
Given the equation: \[(z + 1/z)^2 = 98\] Applying the algebraic identity \((a+b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2\): \[z^2 + 2(z)\left(\frac{1}{z}\right) + \left(\frac{1}{z}\right)^2 = 98\] \[z^2 + 2 + \frac{1}{z^2} = 98\] Subtracting 2 from both sides to isolate the requested expression: \[z^2 + \frac{1}{z^2} = 98 - 2 = 96\] \[\boxed{96}\]
Key points
  • Algebraic Manipulation: For terms involving \(x + 1/x\), squaring the expression is the standard method to derive the values of \(x^2 + 1/x^2\).

questions.question: The roots of \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\) are real and positive. \(a, b\) and \(c\) are real. Then \(ax^2 + b|x| + c = 0\) has
questions.explanation:
Let the roots of \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\) be \(\alpha, \beta\). Given \(\alpha, \beta > 0\) and real. For \(f(x) = ax^2 + b|x| + c = 0\):
  • If \(x \ge 0\), \(|x| = x\), the equation becomes \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), yielding 2 positive roots (\(\alpha, \beta\)).
  • If \(x < 0\), \(|x| = -x\), the equation becomes \(ax^2 - bx + c = 0\). Since \(\alpha, \beta\) are roots of \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), then \(-\alpha, -\beta\) are roots of \(ax^2 - bx + c = 0\). This yields 2 negative roots.
Total real roots = 2 (positive) + 2 (negative) = 4 real roots. \[\boxed{\text{D: 4 real roots}}\]
Key points
  • Symmetry in Absolute Values: If \(f(x)\) is an even function (\(f(x) = f(|x|)\)), then for every positive root \(x_0\), there exists a corresponding negative root \(-x_0\).

questions.question: The Palghat Gap (or Palakkad Gap), a region about 30 km wide in the southern part of the Western Ghats in India, is lower than the hilly terrain to its north and south. The exact reasons for the formation of this gap are not clear. It results in the neighbouring regions of Tamil Nadu getting more rainfall from the South West monsoon and the neighbouring regions of Kerala having higher summer temperatures. What can be inferred from this passage?
options: The Palghat gap is caused by high rainfall and high temperatures in southern Tamil Nadu and Kerala
The regions in Tamil Nadu and Kerala that are near the Palghat Gap are low-lying
The low terrain of the Palghat Gap has a significant impact on weather patterns in neighbouring parts of Tamil Nadu and Kerala
Higher summer temperatures result in higher rainfall near the Palghat Gap area
questions.explanation:
The passage provides specific geographical and meteorological details:
  • The Palghat Gap is lower than the surrounding hilly terrain.
  • This specific topography "results in" neighboring Tamil Nadu receiving more rainfall and Kerala experiencing higher temperatures.
The direct causal link established in the text supports the inference that the gap's low terrain significantly impacts local weather. \[\boxed{\text{C }}\]
Key points
  • Logical Inference: In reading comprehension, an inference must be a direct consequence of the facts stated, without introducing external geographic knowledge.

questions.question: Round-trip tickets to a tourist destination are eligible for a discount of 10% on the total fare. In addition, groups of 4 or more get a discount of 5% on the total fare. If the one way single person fare is Rs 100, a group of 5 tourists purchasing round-trip tickets will be charged Rs _______.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Calculate the base fare for a round trip.
Single person one-way = Rs 100. Base round-trip fare \(= 100 \times 2 = \text{Rs } 200\). Total Base trip fare for 5 person \(Rs \space200 \times(5)= Rs 1000\) Step 2: Apply successive discounts.
  • Round-trip discount (\(10\%\)): \(1000 \times (0.10) = \text{Rs } 100\).
  • Group discount (\(5\%\) for 5 people): \(1000 \times (1 - 0.05) = \text{Rs 50 }\).
Step 3: Total for 5 tourists.
Total charge \(= 1000 -100-50 = 850\). \[\boxed{850}\]
Mistakes to avoid
  • Do not add the percentages (\(10\% + 5\% = 15\%\)). Discounts are usually applied on successively stated otherwise which is told in this case.

questions.question: When a point inside of a tetrahedron (a solid with four triangular surfaces) is connected by straight lines to its corners, how many (new) internal planes are created with these lines? ________
questions.explanation:
A tetrahedron has 4 vertices (\(V_1, V_2, V_3, V_4\)). Let \(P\) be the internal point. Internal planes are formed by connecting \(P\) to any two vertices of the tetrahedron.
  • Each internal plane is defined by the set \(\{P, V_i, V_j\}\).
  • The number of such planes is the number of ways to choose 2 vertices from 4.
\[\text{Number of planes} = 4C2 = \frac{4 \times 3}{2} = 6\] \[\boxed{6}\]

questions.question: What is the average of all multiples of 10 from 2 to 198?
questions.explanation:
The multiples of 10 within the range (2, 198) are: \(10, 20, 30, \dots, 190\) . This sequence is an Arithmetic Progression (AP) where:
  • First term (\(a\)) = 10
  • Last term (\(l\)) = 190
  • Common difference (\(d\)) = 10
The number of terms (\(n\)) is calculated as follows : \[190 = 10 + (n-1)10 \implies 180 = (n-1)10 \implies n = 19\] The average of a linear AP is the mean of the first and last terms : \[\text{Average} = \frac{10 + 190}{2} = \frac{200}{2} = 100\] \[\boxed{\text{B: 100}}\]
Key points
  • AP Averages: In any arithmetic progression, the average is always equivalent to the median or the average of the two extremes .
